text: Good afternoon, everybody. My name is John Pepper. I am the chair of the Student Services Committee, and I call the June 18th, 2026, Student Services Committee meeting to order. Joining me today, as always, are my colleagues, Ms. Carrie Labelle from the Catoctin District and Ms. April Chandler, school board chair from the Algonquin District. We will begin the meeting with public comment, of which

there is none, so we will move directly to the draft minutes from the May 21st, 2026, Student Services Committee meeting. I assume that my colleagues have all had the opportunity to review these minutes, and I will entertain a motion to approve them. Ms. Labelle. I move to approve the minutes from the May 21st meeting of the Student Services Committee. Ms. Chandler? Second.

That motion has been made by Ms. Labelle and seconded by Ms. Chandler. Is there any discussion? Seeing none, all those in favor of approving the draft minutes of the May 21st, 2026, Student Services Committee meeting, please say aye. Aye. Aye. That motion passes unanimously. We will now, as I mentioned in the previous meeting, move ahead from four, which is just the PowerPoint presentation,

to five, which is our action items. The first action item on the agenda is revised Policy 8160, Exception to School Assignment Due to Attendance this policy. Ms. Chandler. Let's see. I move that the Student Services Committee consider

revised Policy 8160, Exceptions to School Assignment Due to Attendance board as an information item. Is there a second? I second. Thank you. That motion was made by Ms. Chandler and seconded by Ms. Labelle. Is there any discussion on revised Policy 8160? Ms. Chandler. Thank you. It's been a little while since we talked about this, so I

just want to make sure that my understanding is in the right place. So, the only significant change to the policy is defining how long the period of late requests will be in play. Yes, ma'am. And so that will be 60 days. And I think we learned a lot about the process. Really, it's been a long time since there's been a significant rezoning. We learned a lot in the process this year.

Could you tell me a little bit about how we plan, in the next round, to make sure that we don't have so many emails going into spam and can better communicate with families? So we will continue to work with Razie on communication, and I think there are enhancements to the survey platform itself that will help alleviate that. We will also do additional messaging through the schools and

through our emails. I believe a lot of the confusion this past year had to do with how the messages were coming as to who they were from. And so that has been resolved. I believe it's now LCPS in the name title itself, so that should help alleviate it. But we'll continue to message. We will probably actually talk about this during the attendance zone change process, too, to say that in a certain amount of time they will, and if you haven't

received or you're wondering, to reach out to us. So we will continue to communicate more and hopefully in a better fashion. Thank you so much for that clarification. Any further discussion? Okay. I do have a few very short questions because I was not part of the full board who went through this process last time. I've seen the downfall of this is

we've had many, many appeals hearings on 8160. When the survey goes out, the survey itself only went out to every student who was affected by the zoning changes. Is that correct? Or is it just those who were juniors, or how did that work? So we survey all eligible students. Okay. So in this instance, we sent a message to rising

seniors because they did not have to move. So if parents wish for those students to go to their new assigned school, which we had a couple, they reached out to us. But we sent messaging to rising juniors as well as rising sophomores based on board direction because they asked us to expand the process. We only noticed the parents, that didn't go to the students. We noticed the parents, both parent one and parent two, their contact of those students who

lived in the zone and were currently attending said school. If you had special permission and you were attending Independence, which was not in the boundary process, we did not survey because they're not there. And so, we did message that way, and then we provided the list of students to each of the principals so at the counseling level, they could do a quick check if they ever had a question so that they could bounce families to us, too, which we discovered did happen. Perfect. I appreciate that.

Was a response required from every student, or was it only required from those students who wanted to remain at the original school and not go to the new school? It was only those who wished to request to remain. If you anticipated your student was going because they had an incoming freshman, then they did not have to respond. Okay. I wonder, and this is just a thought, I'm not saying, because it'd probably be a

lot more work on your part, if a response one way or the other would be required, and that way we could catch those who kind of fell through the cracks. Because I feel like that is what's driving a lot of what has happened with just a lot of people. I think the survey also had a title that wasn't abundantly clear as to what the survey was. So just a couple of changes going forward, because I think this is good policy, I just don't want anyone to fall through the cracks. All right. With that,

any other questions? All right. All those in favor of sending revised policy 8160 to the full board as an information item, please say aye. Aye. Aye. That motion passes unanimously. We will now go to action item 5.02, which is revised policy 5340 on the safe and supportive removal of students, and I will take a motion for this policy.

It's your turn. I move that we send the revised policy 5340, safe and supportive removal of students in the educational setting, to advance to the full board at their next meeting. Is there a second? Oh, second. Okay, thank you, Ms. Chandler. That motion was made by Ms. Lavelle and seconded by Ms. Chandler.
Is there any discussion on new policy 5340?

Ms. Chandler. So I, again, will probably mention this when we talk about it in front of the school board as well. I love the process that we took to create this policy together. And I just found it to be a very effective use of time, and it was great to have lots of invested parties who have strong opinions on this policy at the table, and I found that experience to be very valuable.

I'm just looking a little bit at some of the official SEAC concerns that came back and thought it might be helpful if we talk through some of the concerns and recommendations. So in looking at their recommendation number one to modify line 17 and add the designated supportive area or the removal of the students from the instructional setting, leaving a student

in the instructional setting for the purpose of de-escalation and regulation of a student or students. Could you speak to whether or not staff has a position on that? Certainly. Thank you, Mrs. Chandler, for that question. So when drafting the policy, truly, and working with last year's student services committee, we were really looking at individual students and not necessarily those incidences that might happen

when we have to leave an individual student in a space and then remove the classroom, because that sometimes does happen. We do have notification processes when that happens for the families of the students who did have to leave their classroom space because there was a friend that was in distress. So the focus of this policy is on individual students.

Now, certainly should it be the will of the committee that we consider adding some additional language to also capture those circumstances where we leave the individual student but then have to clear the other students, that could possibly fit within this policy. But I just know that the original lens was on individual students. Sorry.

Chair Pepper. Oh, sorry. Same thing. I just wanted to let you know your microphone was not on. Oh, thank you. And it wasn't me doing it this time. I know. Okay. And then, could we talk about the second recommendation to under Section H, line 91, after future policy revisions, add repeated or patterned use of safe and supportive removal involving an individual student shall trigger an administrative review to determine whether

additional supports, interventions, evaluations, and revisions to the student's plan are necessary. Is that something that would happen anyway? Okay. There we go. So would it naturally happen? I would like to say yes. Might we need to be more prescribed in that happening? I would also say yes. Again, staff have drafted a regulation but have not

previewed that regulation with you all because we weren't sure what changes you might make to the actual policy. So I would think that that is something that we would spell out in regulation as part of the practice, how this policy is implemented. Certainly, we welcome the feedback. Now, again, if it's the will of the committee to add something about if we see a pattern of three or five, you definitely would need to talk about what constitutes a pattern.

We typically, when looking at behavioral incidences, we do a pattern analysis. You're looking at the frequency, you're looking at the type of behavior that triggered the need for the removal to determine whether it truly is a pattern or are they isolated instances. Or would you simply be looking at there's been three safe and supportive removals, there's been five safe and

supportive removals, regardless of what initiated the need for those removals from the educational setting? That is certainly something that the committee could consider. And I do think it would be beneficial for us to give guidance to our school-based teams. Okay. Mm-hmm. Ms. Labelle, do you have a follow-up on this? Yes, I do. Thank you. I was there when they were discussing this at the SEAC meeting,

and they also were concerned with how many. Do we say two, five, seven? And again, they were also naming the same issues that you named. Is this because of the trigger? Is this a different behavior every time? Is it a different time of day, I think they brought up. Are they doing it always the same, like at 10:00 in the morning or 2:00 in the afternoon? So that was something else that they were very concerned

about. So I think if we go ahead and talk about patterns of behavior, that we need to be very clear about this because I think a lot of people could misunderstand and then misuse, not intentionally, but still misuse it. So that would be my recommendation, to look at that very carefully. I would like to ask another follow-up question and really just for

clarifying purposes. There could possibly be a situation where one instance of safe and supportive removal of students could trigger additional-- Is that correct, Ms. Richardson? Absolutely. I would think that we would be looking at the nature of what triggers the need for the removal as to whether or not we pull together an educational planning team to sit down and really look at the

additional needs of that student. Okay. Absolutely. So committee, what do we think about adding something like this and/or the specificity that needs to happen? Ms. Labelle. I think it would be prudent to add verbiage that says that they need

to look at the when, where, and why, and we can adjust the language any way we need to, of the beginning of a crisis so that they are aware of that. And then pull together a team if there has been more than one of these to look and see if something needs to change in it. Is this the beginning of a pattern?

All the things that we just talked about needing to know before we made a determination of what the pattern is. So we need to put that verbiage in there, tell them what they should be looking at before they make any sort of decision about a pattern. I agree with you on some of this. I think if I'm reading recommendation two correctly, what it says is repeated or patterned use, right? So shall trigger an administrative

review to determine whether additional supports or interventions or evaluations. So I think that by saying it's going to trigger the review, I think the analysis piece is in that as to, is it a time of day? Is it a certain trigger? Is it a day of the week? Is it it's rainy outside? So, it could be anything, right? So I think it's written. What I don't like about this, I think is what Ms. Richardson kind of was alluding to, in that

there's a little bit of vagary in repeated or patterned use, right? What does that mean? We need to really spell out. And for me, I'm going to say this, I've worked in education, but I'm not an expert. I don't know. Is three the appropriate amount? Is five the appropriate amount? So maybe I'll ask you all, as you all are the experts, what do you believe would be an appropriate amount? Certainly.

As a practitioner, I would say that three instances of needing to be removed is indicative of a pattern, right? And so then that would trigger us to sit down and look at the antecedent, the actual behavior, and then that follow-up sort of consequence or what we put in place, those supportive measures that we put in place. I think for implementation for staff, it's cleanest if

the committee would consider three removals would then trigger the need for an educational planning team to come together to look at the what, the when, the where, and try to get to the root cause of the why. Ms. Chandler, do you have something? I agree. I think I would be happy- Okay ... with that suggestion. I would like to make an amendment. Okay.

Okay? So what I would like to see, and I'm going to make an amendment, and you guys can second, take it at your word, we can discuss it, is under Section H, after future policy revisions, I would add three uses of safe and supportive removal involving an individual student shall trigger an administrator review to identify repeated or pattern usage

and determine whether additional supports, interventions, evaluations, or revisions to a student's plan is necessary. I'd be happy to second that. Okay. So I have made a motion. It has been seconded by Ms. Chandler. Ms. Richardson, do you need me to state that again? You think you got it? Okay. Any discussion on the amendment? Okay. Seeing no discussion, all of those in favor of the amendment, please say

aye. Aye. That amendment has passed unanimously. Does anyone have anything additional they would like to discuss? Ms. Labelle. Thank you, Mr. Pepper. One other concern, and this might need a whole separate policy or discussion among the board, is that it's one of our classes that are out in the community.

They are community-based, not within the school, and they have a problem, where a child needs to be removed from the rest of the group. We don't have any specific direction for those teachers for actions to take. It might be that one is out someplace with a student doing job observation, job work.

The other teacher has the others in a classroom, so there's still only one teacher there. If anything happened in either place, out in the community or in the community classroom, as it were, we don't have any direction for those people. Do we need to write it into this policy, or do we think we want to look at something totally different because the

actions available to our teachers that are teaching in community locations are different, totally different than what you would do in a school? So noting that this policy is titled Safe and Supportive Removal of Students from the Educational Setting, and assuming that those students who are on a community,

what's the terminology? I want to get the terminology right here, but for those students who are in a community-based program are technically in an educational setting, I feel as if this may fit into this policy. But I'm also going to once again ask our experts who are practitioners in the field to weigh in on this. Certainly. Thank you very much. All of our community-based programs still fall under our LCPS policies because they are our LCPS students. So we have memorandums of understanding with

all of our community-based partners, like our CAST program that's out at Lansdowne or at Salamander, those working through Didlake. We have partnerships, right? And so we also make sure that they have appropriate staffing. So there's a teacher, a job coach, and oftentimes a TA. So no one adult is left alone should a student go into crisis. They would still follow the same expectations by policy and by practice and

training, even in the community-based setting for our students. And we have had incidences that have happened where students have gotten a little overwhelmed and dysregulated, and we've had to remove them from that task, and we do so safely within our programs that are out on their CBIs. Thank you for that. It was a question, there were two teachers

there that actually did have community-based educational settings, and they felt like they really didn't have any specific guidance. Who did they contact? The principal, the special ed department. So if maybe we need a little more clarity to them, I don't know if it needs to be in policy, but certainly communication would help them. Certainly happy to take that concern back to our transition team, and we can make

sure that we provide that explicit training again to our transition teachers and our job coaches. So just for your awareness, should something happen in the community, they are to call a building administrator immediately. Okay. Okay? All righty. Thank you. Yes. Okay. Anything further from the committee? Okay. At this time, I will call the question. All of those in favor of sending this as an information

item to the full school board, please say aye. Aye. Aye. That motion has passed unanimously. That is the end of our action items for this meeting. language. out-of-zone school transfer process. Okay. So it's a different process. So- What process would they have been on in the first place? Because we're really trying to get,

again, that provision of... capacity. Committee members. Committee members, would anybody like to begin? Because I'm happy to start rolling. I had my first question already. Okay. Let's get started. I will happily roll. The first sentence says basically it's over 100% of capacity is over capacity, but then further down it says it's 85%. So I was doing some work on my own

and now I've got to pull it up. I'm going to ask you for just a minute of grace here while I open up the combined that I put in just for this section. I didn't write everything. I did not use blank, no. I'm hoping, and I'm happy to share this with everybody, that that is amenable and much more clarifying than a sentence, unless you know of a reason

why these are two separate paragraphs, and maybe there's a back reason as to why that's different. I'm happy to share that with you all. No, it's the current- Even somebody who is continuing, maybe they were in second grade and they're being allowed to Stay for third grade. So, this policy itself causes that regional placement because the family has moved in, purchased a home, and is expecting to have both of their children
